children: The broader market witnessed mixed performance during the week and underperformed the main indices, with the Nifty Midcap 100 index edging higher to extend its winning streak for the fourth consecutive week. However, the Nifty Smallcap 100 index declined 1%, snapping its three-week gaining streak.

The Nifty Midcap 100 index ended marginally higher, extending its winning streak for the fourth consecutive week. The gains were led by Blue Star, Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA), IDFC First Bank, IndusInd Bank, Exide Industries, Voltas and Fortis Healthcare.

The Nifty Smallcap 100 index declined 1% during the week, snapping its four-week winning streak. Kaynes Technology India, Inox Wind, CreditAccess Grameen, KEC International, Pine Labs, Manappuram Finance, Triveni Turbine and ITI were among the top losers. On the other hand, Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation, SignatureGlobal India, Aptus Value Housing Finance India, Tata Technologies and Indraprastha Gas featured among the notable gainers.
For the week, the BSE Sensex added 2327.26 points, or 2.85 percent, to close at 83,919.71, while the Nifty 50 advanced 656.3 points, or 2.61 percent, to settle at 25,800.60.

"Dalal Street closed the week on a strong footing, with the Nifty and Sensex both notching a fourth consecutive weekly advance and best closing levels in nine months. Over the last four weeks, the Nifty has jumped more than 14%, its sharpest such run in six years. Bank Nifty led from the front, ending at a record 64,635.20 after gaining nearly 6% for the week. Lenders alone accounted for almost nine-tenths of the market value created in the past five sessions," said Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer from Master Capital Services.

"The rally, however, lacked breadth. Midcaps were broadly unchanged, and smallcaps eased roughly 1%, pointing to a market where gains were concentrated in heavyweight stocks. The biggest driver was the return of foreign institutional money. After a prolonged period of net selling, FIIs turned aggressive buyers, putting roughly $10 billion into Indian equities in November alone. Their preference for liquid, large-cap financials explains why the benchmarks and banks outpaced the rest of the market. Softer crude prices provided a second leg of support. Brent has slid sharply from the $117 zone at the end of October to around $92, helped by hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Iran standoff," Singh said.

"Cheaper oil is a clear positive for India, since it trims the import bill, cools inflation risks and eases pressure on the current account. The rupee benefited from both trends, rising to a seven-month high near 93.5 per dollar and emerging as Asia's top-performing currency this month. A firmer currency improves dollar returns for overseas investors and encourages further inflows."

"Global rotation also mattered. A steep sell-off in US and Asian technology shares pushed funds out of AI-linked bets and towards markets with lower exposure to that theme, such as India. The Nifty and Sensex were the only gainers among 12 major global indices this week. A low base also helped, as the Nifty has bounced from an October trough near 22,180," he added further.

Sectorally, PSU banks led the rally, with the Nifty PSU Bank index surging 6.72% during the week, followed by the Nifty Bank and Nifty Private Bank indices, which gained 5.9% and 5.65%, respectively. The Nifty Financial Services and Nifty FMCG indices also advanced 3.65% and 3.63%, respectively. On the other hand, metal stocks were the worst performers, with the Nifty Metal index declining 2.98%, followed by Capital Markets (-1.96%), IT (-1.91%) and India Defence (-1.43%).

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) extended their buying streak for the fourth consecutive week, purchasing equities worth Rs 62,158.14 crore. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) remained net sellers for the third straight week, offloading equities worth Rs 12,698.39 crore, although the pace of selling moderated compared with the previous week.
The total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies increased by nearly Rs 4 lakh crore during the week.
Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities
Nifty on the weekly chart formed a long bull candle after a consolidation movement of last week and settled with weekly gains of 2.6%.

The underlying trend of Nifty remains sharply positive. Having surpassed the hurdle of 25500 this week, Nifty is expected to zoom towards 26000 and next 26350 in the next 1 or 2 weeks. Any consolidation or dips could find support around 25500 as per change in polarity.
Siddhartha Khemka - Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services

Indian equities are expected to sustain their gradual uptrend, underpinned by record FII purchases of ₹1,01,641 crore in November, the highest monthly inflow since Nov’20, amid improving earnings visibility and a stronger rupee, which has appreciated to ₹92.6 against the US dollar to a seven-month high
